heading: A child policy or a child rider? (74 seconds)
name: Children's life insurance: a child policy or a child rider?
description: Two ways to cover a child: a small whole life policy on the child, or a child rider on a parent's term policy. A plain side-by-side look for parents and grandparents.
transcript: Two ways to cover a child with life insurance, side by side. The first way is usually a small whole life policy on the child. A parent or grandparent buys it. The child can keep it as an adult. It locks in insurability. Coverage stays in force while premiums are paid, even if health conditions appear later. It builds cash value slowly. The second way is a child rider on a parent's term policy. If you buy term life, you may be able to add one for all your children. It usually can be converted to the child's own policy later. A child policy is permanent. The child can keep it. A rider is often enough when the goal is simply protection during childhood. A child depends on your income far more than you depend on a policy on the child. So parents should have their own coverage in place first. A child's whole life policy is not a college savings plan. Its cash value grows slowly in the first decade. If saving for education is the goal, compare dedicated options too. Want to talk it through?
